lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: A fossil so strange scientists still can't agree what it was.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: 1955, Illinois. An amateur collector finds a fossil and takes it to the Field Museum. The experts are stumped.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: It's about 300 million years old. Up to 35 centimetres long. A cigar-shaped body, a tail fin, and eyes on two stalks. And a long snout with a tiny claw at the end.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: It was named in 1966. In 1989, Illinois made it the state fossil.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: In 2016, two papers said it was a vertebrate, related to fish like lampreys. In 2017, another team replied that it was not.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Since then: chemistry studies lean toward a chordate. A 2023 scan study doubts several of the vertebrate features. Still unsettled.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Thousands of fossils. One verdict, missing. Gloom: "Science is thorough. Eventually."
